blockingIssues.problem: The title asserts a universal next-step decision (“Fix Narrative first in the next pipeline trial”), but the source does not support a universal rule to always fix Narrative first. The report explicitly says drift can originate in Idea or Synthesis and recommends targeting “the first stage supported by the evidence for the chosen failure,” noting that Narrative is the most recurrent locus but not always the earliest locus.
blockingIssues.sourceEvidence: “Drift is not confined to Idea.”; “Narrative is the most recurrent first visible hierarchy shift in the available records.”; “Do not infer that another Idea-only change or a Compose-only style change will address every failure. The next useful experiment should be one controlled upstream-boundary trial that: 1. Targets the first stage supported by the evidence for the chosen failure (Narrative is the most recurrent locus; compare its actual Synthesis input before changing it).” ; “Experiment 007 already demonstrates Synthesis-origin drift in one run; Experiment 008 demonstrates Idea-origin drift; Experiment 009 shows downstream drift despite a company-first Idea.”
blockingIssues.constraint: The source supports selecting the intervention point based on which stage the evidence actually localizes as first for the chosen failure; it does not support an unconditional rule that Narrative must always be fixed first.
